episode_title: The Secret to Building a Business That Makes Money On Autopilot - Cassandra Smith #150

real_qa.q: How did Cassandra Smith generate $86,000 in revenue in May 2020 after earning only $10,000 in 2020 before that breakthrough?
real_qa.r: Cassandra shifted her approach from trying to sell products directly to teaching people the skill of making t-shirts. She started going live on camera every day with intention after a personal crisis moment. She mastered communication by learning to sell the outcome and results of her courses rather than the product itself. When she did that field team dollars per year in 2020 and then made $86,000 in May 2020, she knew she was going to be unstoppable.

real_qa.q: What role did Cassandra Smith's son play in preventing her from leaving the hotel during her darkest moment in 2020?
real_qa.r: When Cassandra was in a hotel in 2020 and considering taking her own life, she planned to ask her son if he wanted to stay with his grandmother. However, her son refused to leave her, saying 'no, I'm not going anywhere' and asking 'what we got to do?' His refusal to abandon her became the turning point that made her realize she needed to find a way to make money and survive. She then turned on her camera to go live with the intention that she had a reason to still be here and to still live.

real_qa.q: What was Cassandra Smith's first revenue milestone that convinced her to quit her job in 2019?
real_qa.r: Cassandra made her first $1,000 in a week while still working her job and making t-shirts. When she realized she could make $1,000 while only working part-time on the business, she thought about what she could do if she worked full-time. This led her to quit her job in 2019, though the t-shirt business subsequently declined and she ended up homeless, which pushed her to pivot to teaching others the skill.

real_qa.q: How did Freedom Digital Academy grow to over 18,000 entrepreneurs in its free community?
real_qa.r: Cassandra created Freedom Digital Academy as a free community after discovering that people didn't want to buy t-shirts but instead wanted to learn how to make them. She focused on teaching people to monetize their existing skills rather than learning new things. The community grew to over 18,000 entrepreneurs by emphasizing mindset work and personal vulnerability alongside practical skills, pushing mindset and value first before the sale.

real_qa.q: Why did Cassandra Smith's approach shift from selling t-shirt products to teaching people how to make t-shirts?
real_qa.r: When Cassandra went live on camera to try to sell t-shirts directly, everyone on the live stream asked her how to make t-shirts instead of buying them. She realized she needed to teach people the skill, saying 'let me start trying to sell people their fish and teach them how to fish, they sell.' She discovered that when she learned to master communication and sell the outcome of what the class would do for people's lives rather than the product itself, her business went wild.
real_qa.requete: Cassandra Smith pivot teaching t-shirts skill

guest.bio_context: Cassandra Smith is a mother and entrepreneur who built a multi-million dollar digital business from a hotel room during the COVID-19 pandemic. She dropped out of high school at age 18 after having two children and worked temp service jobs before transitioning to digital entrepreneurship. She created Freedom Digital Academy, a free community with over 18,000 entrepreneurs, and has generated over eight figures in sales through teaching others how to monetize their skills online.
